item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays entered 2026 expecting their offence to help carry them to another postseason run. Instead, a lineup that had been central to the club’s World Series appearance a year earlier became one of its biggest weaknesses. Established stars endured dramatic downturns, useful role players were asked to carry larger workloads and injuries forced Toronto to lean on several inexperienced hitters.
Anyone who watched the Blue Jays in 2026 knows they were not a good offensive team. They scored the fewest runs in all of baseball (648), hit the fewest home runs (152), and ranked second-worst in team OPS (.691) ahead of only the Los Angeles Angels.
There were still a few encouraging performances. But for every one of those successes they Blue Jays had another two or three hitters who fell short of expectations. The grades below weigh each hitter’s production against his role, opportunity and expectations entering the season.
Grading every Blue Jays hitter from the 2026 season
Alejandro Kirk
- HR: 10
- RBI: 43
- AVG: .278
- OPS: .767
- wRC+: 114
Kirk didn’t look like himself to start the year, then missed several months with a thumb injury. He recaptured his All-Star form when he finally returned, however, and led the Blue Jays offensively for much of the second half.
Grade: B+
Andrés Giménez
- HR: 9
- RBI: 59
- AVG: .244
- OPS: .649
- wRC+: 81
Giménez is what he is at this point: a below-average hitter with a knack for coming through in the clutch. He still managed to accrue 2.8 fWAR on the strength of his stellar glovework at shortstop and contributions on the basepaths.
Grade: B-
Brandon Valenzuela
- HR: 9
- RBI: 24
- AVG: .226
- OPS: .688
- wRC+: 96
Valenzuela filled in admirably for Kirk while he was on the injured list during the first half of the season. He flashed legitimate power upside at the plate before going ice-cold after the All-Star break, exposing the current limitations of his offensive profile.
Grade: C
Brett Bateman
- HR: 2
- RBI: 11
- AVG: .329
- OPS: .826
- wRC+: 138
Bateman exceeded all expectations after being acquired for Kevin Gausman at the trade deadline. He injected some life into the lineup immediately upon arrival and has likely cemented himself as a marquee piece of the 2027 squad.
Grade: A+
Charles McAdoo
- HR: 3
- RBI: 14
- AVG: .258
- OPS: .694
- wRC+: 93
McAdoo largely held his own at the plate with the Blue Jays in 2026. His approach needs work, but his combination of power and speed is exciting. He should keep improving with additional reps against MLB pitching.
Grade: C+
Davis Schneider
- HR: 5
- RBI: 16
- AVG: .145
- OPS: .624
- wRC+: 84
Schneider was one of several surprise contributors who propelled the Blue Jays to the World Series in 2025. His production fell off a cliff this year, which led to multiple demotions to Triple-A Buffalo. He might be out of runway.
Grade: F
Ernie Clement
- HR: 9
- RBI: 48
- AVG: .259
- OPS: .649
- wRC+: 80
It was a tale of two seasons for Clement. He rode a strong first half to his first career All-Star appearance, then devolved into one of baseball’s worst hitters from August onward. He ended the year with the worst offensive numbers of his career.
Grade: C-
George Springer
- HR: 15
- RBI: 54
- AVG: .249
- OPS: .726
- wRC+: 105
Springer redeemed what was likely his final season with the Blue Jays with a strong second half. While he didn’t come anywhere near his 2025 numbers, he still put together a solid season. His contract was worth every penny.
Grade: B-
Jésus Sánchez
- HR: 8
- RBI: 35
- AVG: .254
- OPS: .713
- wRC+: 99
He makes the list because he was on the team for most of the year before being designated for assignment in September. He failed to turn his power potential into actual production, and the less that can be said about his defence, the better.
Grade: D
Josh Smith
- HR: 6
- RBI: 15
- AVG: .203
- OPS: .611
- wRC+: 75
Smith was a pleasant surprise down the stretch after coming over in the Adam Macko trade, hitting five of his six home runs after coming to Toronto. He should have an opportunity to compete for a bench spot on the 2027 squad.
Grade: B-
Kazuma Okamoto
- HR: 33
- RBI: 92
- AVG: .232
- OPS: .762
- wRC+: 113
The general consensus on Okamoto coming over from Japan was that he would hit for a high average with some power. He ended up being more of a three true outcome guy who led the team in home runs, RBI, and strikeouts by a wide margin.
Grade: B+
Myles Straw
- HR: 3
- RBI: 26
- AVG: .241
- OPS: .646
- wRC+: 83
Straw wound up getting far more plate appearances than anyone expected he would coming into the year. Unsurprisingly, he didn’t do much with those opportunities. His value is in his speed, excellent defensive play, and clubhouse presence.
Grade: C+
Nathan Lukes:
- HR: 10
- RBI: 41
- AVG: .277
- OPS: .725
- wRC+: 102
Lukes got off to an extremely rough start at the plate while managing a bout of vertigo, but eventually settled back into his usual form. He’s a league-average hitter who grinds out at-bats—a quintessentially glue guy in a deeper lineup.
Grade: B
Sean Keys
- HR: 2
- RBI: 9
- AVG: .197
- OPS: .570
- wRC+: 57
Assigning Keys a letter grade almost feels unfair given how little he played. Still, he flashed some power potential in his limited opportunities, albeit while appearing generally overmatched by major league pitching. He’s very much a work in progress.
Grade: C
Vladimir Guerrero Jr.
- HR: 9
- RBI: 57
- AVG: .260
- OPS: .688
- wRC+: 95
This might be the most disappointing season by a hitter in the 50-year history of the franchise. Coming off a historic postseason, Guerrero authored one of the most pathetic performances by a superstar in recent memory. That ridiculous quote didn’t help, either.
Grade: F

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

28 Sep 2026, 10:25 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Ed Szczepanski)
Rookie Lucas Spence ripped a two-run triple to highlight a four-run third inning, helping the Houston Astros celebrate the American League West title with a 9-0 victory over the Athletics on Sunday in West Sacramento, Calif.
Christian Walker homered to lead off the sixth inning and joined Yainer Diaz, Cam Smith and Jeremy Pena in collecting two hits and an RBI for the Astros (81-81), who won the division for the eighth time in the last 10 seasons.
Third-seeded Houston will host the Chicago White Sox on Tuesday in Game 1 of the best-of-three wild-card series. The Astros went 5-2 against the White Sox this season.
Houston actually captured the AL West title prior to the conclusion of its victory, as the Texas Rangers dropped a 6-4 decision to the Minnesota Twins on Sunday.
Yordan Alvarez went 1-for-4 with an RBI single to boost his batting average to .316, giving him his first batting title.
Lawrence Butler had two of the five hits for the Athletics (64-98), who lost for the ninth time in 12 games.
Phillies 7, Tampa Bay 3
Zack Wheeler pitched six strong innings and Kyle Schwarber drove in two runs as the Phillies clinched their fifth straight postseason berth by beating the Rays.
Bryce Harper and Edmundo Sosa homered for Philadelphia, which had lost its previous four games by the combined score of 23-3. The Phillies finally showed signs of life in Game 162, and now they'll head to Atlanta to face the Braves in the National League wild-card round that begins on Tuesday,
Johnny DeLuca homered twice for Tampa Bay. The Rays earned a bye into the American League Division Series and face the winner of the wild-card series between the New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox.
Cubs 6, Red Sox 2
Alex Bregman went 4-for-4 with two home runs and four RBIs against his former team to help Chicago wrap up the regular season by defeating Boston in St. Petersburg, Fla.
The game was scheduled to be played in Boston, but was moved to Tropicana Field because of the nor'easter that hit much of New England throughout the weekend.
Both of Bregman's home runs came against Boston starter Tanner Houck, who made his first appearance on the mound since May 2025. Houck (0-1), who had Tommy John surgery last year, allowed three runs on four hits in three innings. The Red Sox were held to five hits and were 0-for-7 with runners in scoring position.
Twins 6, Rangers 4
Josh Bell hit a two-run home run and drove in three to lead host Minnesota to a season-ending win over Texas.
The loss eliminated the Rangers from the American League West title race and the playoffs. Rangers starter Mackenzie Gore allowed one hit and one run in 2 1/3 innings.
Twins starter Dean Kremer (5-5) gave up three hits and one run in seven innings. Kremer yielded a home run to Danny Jansen, but did not allow another Texas runner past first base.
Dodgers 5, Giants 1 (10 innings)
Andy Pages capped a four-run 10th inning with a three-run home run, and visiting Los Angeles beat San Francisco to earn its 100th win of the season.
The Dodgers took the lead in the 10th when Alex Call's two-out double off the left field fence drove in automatic runner Miguel Rojas. The Giants then elected to walk Max Muncy, before Pages foiled that strategy by driving a pitch by Duncan Davitt (0-1) into the left field bleachers for his 23rd home run of the season.
Alex Vesia (3-1), whose perfect ninth sent the game into the 10th, was credited with the win, which allows the Dodgers to take a three-game winning streak into their National League Division Series opener next Saturday against the winner of the wild-card series between the host Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies.
Marlins 5, Braves 3
Heriberto Hernandez and Griffin Conine slugged solo home runs, giving host Miami a win over Atlanta to end its season on a high note.
Marlins ace Sandy Alcantara tossed a scoreless ninth inning for his third career save. It was a fitting end of the year for Alcantara, who threw both the first and last pitch of the season for Miami. sStarter Janson Junk left with a no-decision. He allowed three hits and one run in 4 2/3 innings. Michael Petersen (4-4) earned the win with 1 1/3 hitless innings of relief.
Braves starter JR Ritchie (1-5) took the loss. He allowed seven hits and four runs in 5 2/3 innings. Mauricio Dubon hit his 12th homer to open the scoring and added an RBI single for Atlanta, which begins its home wild-card series against divisional rival Philadelphia on Tuesday.
Nationals 6, Mets 4
Andres Chaparro had three hits, including two solo home runs, and host Washington beat New York to end its season with a series win.
Will Dion (3-2) pitched two scoreless innings for the victory and Erik Tolman worked the ninth for his fifth save for Washington, which improved by 11 wins over 2025.
Francisco Lindor hit his 300th career homer and Ronny Mauricio smacked his third home run in two games for the Mets, who finished last in the National League East. Carson Benge ended his rookie season with three hits and an RBI.
Blue Jays 5, Reds 1
In potentially his final career start, Max Scherzer struck out seven over seven-plus innings and host Toronto topped Cincinnati.
The 42-year-old Scherzer (4-9) allowed one run and six hits to earn his 225th career win and boost his strikeout total to 3,557. The Blue Jays' 37-year-old designated hitter George Springer, who might have also played his last game, like Scherzer received a standing ovation when he was replaced.
Brandon Valenzuela hit a two-run home run for Toronto and Charles McAdoo added a solo shot in the rubber match of the three-game series. Brandon Williamson (5-5) allowed four runs and four hits in three innings for the Reds.
White Sox 4, Rockies 2
Randal Grichuk and Brenton Doyle smacked two-run home runs and Anthony Kay pitched five strong innings to boost host Chicago past Colorado.
The White Sox are set to visit the American League West champion Houston Astros on Tuesday in the opener of an AL wild-card series. Chicago clinched its first playoff berth on Thursday since 2021 but was eliminated from contention for an AL Central title with Saturday's loss to Colorado and a Cleveland victory at Kansas City.
Cole Carrigg homered for Colorado, which finished with more than 100 losses for the fourth successive season.
Royals 3, Guardians 2
Vinnie Pasquantino's second solo homer of the day broke an eighth-inning tie and sent host Kansas City to a win over Cleveland.
Jac Caglianone and Kyle Isbel each had two hits for the Royals, who ended a disappointing 2026 campaign by avoiding a sweep and winning for just the seventh time in the final 25 games.
Daniel Schneemann and Jo Adell each homered and had two hits apiece for the Guardians, who rested key regulars Steven Kwan, Jose Ramirez and Brayan Rocchio one day after securing their third consecutive American League Central title. Cleveland plays either the Chicago White Sox or Houston Astros in the American League Division Series.
Pirates 4, Tigers 2
Jared Jones pitched four innings of one-hit ball and Konnor Griffin led off the game with a solo home run and drove in two runs to lead Pittsburgh past host Detroit.
Griffin's homer was the sixth of his rookie season and helped the Pirates secure their first winning record since 2018 and only their second since last making the postseason in 2015. Jones was not eligible for the win after exiting the game before the fifth. Jones finished 5-6 with a 3.72 ERA in 21 starts after returning from elbow surgery in late May.
Rookie River Ryan (0-1) made his second start for the Tigers and sixth of his career. The right-hander allowed two runs on three hits over 1 1/3 innings. Detroit finished with a losing record after advancing to the American League Division Series each of the past two seasons.
Padres 9, Diamondbacks 4
Gavin Sheets homered and Freddy Fermin knocked in three runs as host San Diego tuned up for their National League wild-card series by stopping visiting Arizona.
San Diego, which opens its best-of-three series Tuesday night against the visiting Chicago Cubs, snapped a 4-4 tie with three runs in the bottom of the seventh. Fermin capped it with a two-run single.
Michael Soroka pitched 4 2/3 innings for Arizona, which was eliminated from postseason contention when Philadelphia beat Tampa Bay around the same time San Diego's Jake Cronenworth drew a bases-loaded walk to push home the go-ahead run in the seventh.
Brewers 6, Cardinals 4
Jacob Misiorowski strengthened his case for the National League Cy Young Award, allowing just two hits over five-plus scoreless innings, as host Milwaukee beat St. Louis to close with five consecutive wins and its franchise record for victories in a season (103).
Misiorowski (16-5) allowed two singles in 5 1/3 innings and lowered his major league-leading ERA to 1.80. The right-hander struck out five, giving him 252 strikeouts for the year.
Cardinals starter Andre Pallante (12-9) allowed six runs on 10 hits in five innings. He allowed six singles in the first inning for a 3-0 Brewers lead as well as Gary Sanchez's home run in the third.
Mariners 7, Angels 4
Logan Gilbert pitched four-plus hitless innings and struck out eight as host Seattle dealt Los Angeles its 100th loss of the season. It was also the last game for Dan Wilson as the Mariners' manager. The team announced after the game that Wilson will not return in that role in 2027 after a disappointing season and third-place finish in the American League West.
Jose Siri homered for the Angels, losers of 100 games for the first time. They had been the lone active MLB team to never suffer that many defeats.
Gilbert didn't allow a baserunner until walking Moises Ballesteros leading off the fifth. He struck out the side in the first inning to reach 200 strikeouts for the season, becoming the fourth pitcher in franchise history to do so in multiple seasons.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays are heading into game 162 of the MLB regular season with their tails between their legs. They will play their final game against the Cincinnati Reds, instead of moving through the playoffs with a World Series Title in sight. The Toronto Blue Jays news of the day involves Brandon Valenzuela.
The final game of the year, on Sunday, September 27th, 2026, will be broadcast at 1:07 PM Mountain Time, 3:07 PM Eastern Time. Max Scherzer will take the mound one last time, going against Brandon Williamson.
Toronto Blue Jays fans can tune in to Sportsnet, TVA Sports, and on the radio on SN590 THE FAN.
Toronto Blue Jays Announce Final Brandon Valenzuela Decision For Last Game Against The Cincinnati Reds
Before the first pitch of the final game of the 2026 season, the Blue Jays announced a final decision on Valenzuela.
This is the lineup that the Blue Jays announced for their final game:
- DH: George Springer
- RF: Brett Bateman
- 3B: Kazuma Okamoto
- 1B: Charles McAdoo
- LF: Davis Schneider
- C: Brandon Valenzuela
- CF: Myles Straw
- SS: Andres Gimenez
- 2B: Ernie Clement
Starting Pitcher: Max Scherzer
As you can see from the Blue Jays announcement, Alejandro Kirk has been replaced by Valenzuela for Sunday’s final game. It will be the 25-year-old‘s 91st game of the year.
Additionally, George Springer, Charles McAdoo, Davis Schneider, and Myles Straw are also coming into the lineup. Coming out in their place are Nathan Lukes, Sean Keys, and Josh Smith.
Looking At Brandon Valenzuela & Alejandro Kirk
Valenzuela has been a solid contributor for the Blue Jays this season.
The young catcher has recorded 53 hits, 22 RBIs, two stolen bases, nine doubles, 28 walks, and eight home runs in 90 games. He started 83 games at catcher and five games at first base.
On the other hand, Kirk has been one of the bright spots of the Blue Jays’ otherwise down year.
In 79 games, the 27-year-old recorded 77 hits, eight doubles, 43 RBIs, one stolen base, 33 walks, and 10 home runs.
Brandon Valenzuela’s Future With The Toronto Blue Jays
Valenzuela’s future with the Blue Jays is uncertain.
However, if Springer moves on from Toronto, there will be room for Valenzuela. Kirk has been a better hitter than Valenzuela, making him an easy choice to slide into the designated hitter role. However, if Valenzuela improves his swing, he could spend some games at DH, too.
Valenzuela has pre-arbitration for two years after earning $734,096 in 2026.
One way or another, Valenzuela will be an active member of the Blue Jays for at least another year.

item.content:encoded:
Las Grandes Ligas comienzan a llegar a su fin. Con octubre a la vuelta de la esquina, los equipos de la MLB arrancan el camino rumbo al sueño de la Serie Mundial, desafortunadamente, para algunos equipos significa el fin del camino, caso de ello el de los Toronto Blue Jays, quienes sorpresivamente quedaron fuera de los Playoffs de la Liga Americana.
Referentes de México fuera
Pese a ser uno de los mejores equipos el año pasado, los Azulejos de Toronto no lograron encontrar el ritmo durante la temporada, dejando una marca de 77-81 y quedando matemáticamente eliminado de su zona.
La novena que cuenta con mexicanos como referentes, tales como: Alejandro Kirk, Brandon Valenzuela y José Rodríguez, quedó fuera oficialmente luego de caer ante los Orioles en su Juego 3 y siendo barridos en la serie.
Toronto llegó a este tramo de la temporada con pocas posibilidades de mantenerse con vida en la pelea por un boleto a la Postemporada. La novena canadiense no logró repetir el protagonismo que tuvo durante la campaña anterior y terminó alejándose de los puestos que daban acceso a octubre.
Para los mexicanos, la eliminación significa también el final de su participación en la campaña. Alejandro Kirk volvió a ser una de las piezas mexicanas más reconocidas dentro de la organización, aunque sufrió una importante lesión a mitad de campaña, mientras que Brandon Valenzuela y José Rodríguez fueron poco más frecuentes.
De la Serie Mundial a quedar fuera
El contraste es importante para los Blue Jays, pues después de disputar la Serie Mundial en 2025, el equipo no consiguió mantenerse en la pelea por el campeonato durante esta temporada. La novena canadiense perdió terreno conforme avanzó el calendario y terminó sin posibilidades de regresar a la lucha por el título.
Ahora, Kirk, Valenzuela y Rodríguez deberán esperar al próximo año para volver a buscar un lugar en la Postemporada de las Grandes Ligas. Mientras tanto, Toronto tendrá que comenzar a planear una temporada baja en la que buscará recuperar el nivel mostrado el año pasado.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

24 Sep 2026, 02:25 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Jamie LeBlanc)
Baltimore's Pete Alonso hit another home run and the Orioles eliminated the visiting Toronto Blue Jays from playoff contention by winning 4-2 on Wednesday afternoon in the first game of a doubleheader.
The Blue Jays (77-81) were the reigning American League champions, but they won't have a chance to return to the World Series.
The Orioles (77-81) must win the nightcap of the day-night twinbill in order to stay alive for an AL wild-card spot, though if the Chicago White Sox win in Kansas City later Wednesday, that would bump Baltimore from contention.
Chris Bassitt (9-5) pitched five-plus innings to notch a victory in his third consecutive start. He was charged with two runs on seven hits with one walk.
Andrew Kittredge, the fourth reliever for the Orioles, worked the ninth for his 11th save.
Max Scherzer (3-9) took the loss as he was charged with four runs and four hits in five innings.
Ernie Clement and Andres Gimenez both had two hits, including a double each, for the Blue Jays. Toronto finished with 10 hits, leaving eight runners on base.
The doubleheader was necessary after Tuesday night's scheduled game was postponed.
Jeremiah Jackson's single gave Baltimore the game's first run in the second. Colton Cowser later scored when Jackson was caught attempting to steal second base.
Alonso's two-run blast pushed the margin to 4-0 in the fifth inning. His 41st homer of the season was his third of the series, which began with his two-homer outing Monday night when the Orioles rallied for a 4-3 victory.
Toronto scored two runs on the same play in the sixth inning, both charged to Bassitt. Brandon Valenzuela's two-out infield single pushed in a run and second baseman Jackson's throwing error allowed a second run to score.
Alonso's homer was one of five Baltimore hits. The others were singles. The Orioles won Monday's game with six hits.
Three Toronto relievers limited Baltimore to no runs with one hit.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays are in the middle of a three-game series against the Baltimore Orioles.
The Orioles won the first game of the series 4-3 on Monday. Game 2 was postponed due to inclement weather, and the series will finish with a doubleheader on Wednesday.
The first game of the doubleheader is scheduled to start at 1:35 p.m. EDT. The second game will begin at 6:35 p.m. EDT.
The Blue Jays announced their lineup for the first game of the doubleheader, and it includes a notable decision involving Vladimir Guerrero Jr.
Toronto Blue Jays Make Vladimir Guerrero Jr. Decision Amid Orioles Series
Guerrero is out of the lineup for the second straight game for the first game of the doubleheader on Wednesday.
The first baseman was removed from Sunday’s win over the Texas Rangers with lower back tightness, according to MLB.com’s Keegan Matheson.
Update: Guerrero is now IN the lineup.
Here is Toronto’s lineup for Wednesday afternoon’s game:
- Nathan Lukes RF
- Vladimir Guerrero Jr. 1B
- Kazuma Okamoto 3B
- George Springer DH
- Josh Smith LF
- Andres Gimenez SS
- Brandon Valenzuela C
- Myles Straw CF
- Ernie Clement 2B
SP: RHP Max Scherzer (3-8, 6.07 ERA, 54 SO)
Here is the Orioles’ lineup:
- Dylan Beavers LF
- Pete Alonso 1B
- Gunnar Henderson SS
- Coby Mayo DH
- Edwin Encarnacion-Strand 3B
- Colton Cowser CF
- Jeremiah Jackson 2B
- Leody Taveras RF
- Carlos Narvaez C
SP: RHP Chris Bassitt (8-5, 4.64 ERA, 72 SO)
Looking at Vladimir Guerrero Jr.’s Season
Guerrero has easily had the worst season of his career, posting 1.2 fWAR and a 97 wRC+ with just nine home runs and 56 RBI over 141 games.
In Guerrero’s defense, he has dealt with numerous injuries this year that he played through. His back has bothered him much of the season, and he also dealt with a hamstring issue earlier this season. Not to mention, he missed games with a concussion.
Since making his MLB debut in 2019, Guerrero has posted 21.8 fWAR and a 132 wRC+ with 192 home runs and 647 RBI. The first baseman signed a 14-year, $500 million contract extension with Toronto in spring 2025.
Toronto Blue Jays Right Now
One year after making it to the World Series, Toronto has a 77-80 record.
The Blue Jays haven’t been officially eliminated yet, but just one more loss from the club will seal their fate.
Even if they win out, they’d need a ton of help from around the league to sneak into the playoffs.

The Toronto Blue Jays playoff hopes hang by a thread. That thread will face a razor-sharp challenge in a Baltimore Orioles double-header. However, the other Blue Jays news of the day involves Brandon Valenzuela.
The first game of their doubleheader involves Max Scherzer taking the mound for the Blue Jays. He will go up against Chris Bassitt at 11:35 AM Mountain Time, 1:35 PM Eastern Time.
Toronto Blue Jays News: Brandon Valenzuela In, Alejandro Kirk Out For Game 1 Against The Baltimore Orioles
Prior to the first pitch of today’s doubleheader, the Blue Jays announced their lineup. That lineup marks Valenzuela’s return.
Here is the lineup that the Blue Jays announced:
- RF: Nathan Lukes
- LF: Josh Smith
- 3B: Kazuma Okamoto
- DH: George Springer
- 1B: Sean Keys
- SS: Andres Gimenez
- C: Brandon Valenzuela
- CF: Myles Straw
- 2B: Ernie Clement
Starting Pitcher: Max Scherzer.
“Let’s play TWO! #BlueJays50,” the team announced.
This lineup obviously includes Valenzuela in addition to Myles Straw. The 25-year-old is coming in for Alejandro Kirk, who is coming out. Brett Bateman is missing the game due to injury.
Looking At Brandon Valenzuela
Valenzuela and Kirk have been sharing home plate all season. Between injuries and hot/cold play, it hasn’t been that difficult for John Schneider to shuffle the deck once in a while.
Valenzuela was first acquired by the Blue Jays in July 2025.
“OFFICIAL: We’ve acquired C Brandon Valenzuela from the Padres in exchange for INF Will Wagner. Welcome to our Blue Jays family!” the team announced over a year ago.
Valenzuela played 26 games with the Buffalo Bisons after his acquisition last year. In those games, he recorded 19 hits, six doubles, 12 RBIs, and three home runs.
Fast forward to this season, and Valenzuela has 51 hits, nine doubles, two stolen bases, 21 RBIs, and eight home runs in 88 games.
Looking at Alejandro Kirk
Of all the things that have been going wrong lately, Kirk has been one of the things going right.
The 27-year-old has nine hits, six RBIs, and one home run in his last seven games. In those games, Kirk has a .346 batting average and a .433 on-base percentage.
With these two behind the plate for the Blue Jays for the foreseeable future, Toronto will be well taken care of.

item.content:encoded:
A falta de una semana para que termine la temporada regular en la MLB, el panorama de playoffs comienza a definirse y con ello te presentamos aquellos peloteros mexicanos que ya aseguraron su clasificación a playoffs y quienes todavía están en la pelea por entrar a la postemporada.
Mexicanos que ya aseguraron su pase a postemporada
La presencia de peloteros mexicanos en las últimas ediciones de los playoffs ha sido constante y este año no será la excepción pues hasta ahorita se tiene confirmada la participación de cuatro peloteros mexicanos y dos con estatus todavía pendiente, ya que uno está en sucursales y el otro se encuentra en lista de lesionados.
PUBLICIDAD
A continuación, te presentamos la lista de jugadores nacionales que estarán en los playoffs:
Jonathan Aranda (Tampa Bay Rays)
Ha firmado su campaña más sólida y consagratoria en MLB. Con 149 juegos jugados, el infielder presume un promedio de bateo de .277, conectando 156 imparables, 22 cuadrangulares y remolcando 92 carreras, convirtiéndose en una pieza medular en el lineup de los Rays.
Jarren Durán (Boston Red Sox):
Se ha consolidado como un auténtico motor en los senderos y el jardín central. A lo largo de la temporada suma 20 jonrones, 69 carreras impulsadas y 19 bases robadas en 145 encuentros, destacando además por su velocidad con 5 triples.
PUBLICIDAD
Joey Ortiz (Milwaukee Brewers):
Ha sido una de las grandes revelaciones del año tras su llegada a Milwaukee, aportando una defensa de élite en el cuadro y un bateo sumamente oportuno que ayudó a los Brewers a amarrar temprano su boleto a octubre.
Patrick Sandoval (Boston Red Sox):
El lanzador que representó a México en el Clásico Mundial de Beisbol regresó esta temporada tras un periodo largo fuera de las canchas y ha tenido altibajos con los Boston Red Sox con una efectividad de 5.15 y un récord de 1-7.
Manuel Rodríguez (Tampa Bay Rays):
El lanzador yucateco venía sumando valiosos relevos con efectividad de 3.86 y 8 ponches en el bullpen de Tampa Bay en los cuatro juegos que disputó.
PUBLICIDAD
No obstante, Manuel Rodríguez se encuentra actualmente en la lista de lesionados (IL) de 15 días debido a una distensión en la espalda baja (low back strain), por lo que el cuerpo técnico espera su evolución para ver si podrá estar listo en las primeras rondas de los playoffs.
Alek Thomas (Oklahoma City Comets):
Después de haber sido cambiado desde los Arizona Diamondbacks a inicios de año, el jardinero Alek Thomas se encuentra actualmente en las sucursales de Los Angeles Dodgers
Aunque tuvo una breve participación de 7 juegos con el primer equipo de los Dodgers bateando para .211, la tremenda profundidad del roster angelino ha hecho que se mantenga buscando ritmo en el sistema de ligas menores, a la espera de un llamado que lo devuelva al roster de postemporada.
PUBLICIDAD
Peloteros mexicanos todavía buscan entrar a la postemporada
La presencia de peloteros mexicanos aumentará conforme avance la semana, con varios representantes en equipos que continúan en competencia por buscar entrar a los playoffs.
Toronto Blue Jays cuenta con Alejandro Kirk, Tibo Rodríguez, Brandon Valenzuela y Luis Urías. Por su parte, Randy Arozarena y Andrés Muñoz forman parte de los Seattle Mariners.
Isaac Paredes representa a los Houston Astros, mientras Javier Assad se encuentra con los Chicago Cubs. Alejandro Osuna integra el roster de los Texas Rangers.
Taijuan Walker juega con los Philadelphia Phillies y Jeremiah Estrada pertenece a los San Diego Padres.
Cada uno luchará hasta el último segundo por entrar a la postemporada.

Estados Unidos.- Los mexicanos José Ignacio Rodríguez, Brandon Valenzuela y Alejandro Osuna tuvieron destacada participación en la jornada de este domingo 20 de septiembre de 2026 en las Grandes Ligas, durante el juego que ganaron los Azulejos de Toronto por 7-2 a los Rangers de Texas.
El “Tiburón” Rodríguez, pitcher de los Blue Jays de Toronto originario de Oaxaca, lanzó la séptima entrada en blanco dos días después de su debut en Major League Baseball (MLB), mientras que el oriundo de Los Mochis, Alex Osuna, pegó 2 hits en 4 turnos por parte de los Rangers de Texas, en tanto que Brandon Valenzuela se fue de 3-1 también como parte de los canadienses.
Buen relevo del “Tibu” Rodríguez con los Toronto Blue Jays
Después de debutar el pasado 18 de septiembre con una entrada y tercios en blanco, con un hit y dos ponches ante los Rangers, José Ignacio Rodríguez volvió a la acción este domingo en el estadio Globe Life Field en territorio texano.
Sugerimos: ¡Debut mexicano! José Rodríguez se estrena con Azulejos de Toronto en Grandes Ligas
El “Tibu” ingresó al montículo en el séptimo inning y trabajó una entrada completa de un imparable y un chocolate, para mantener su efectividad en 0.00. Rodríguez inició su labor con un hit en contra de parte de Evan Carter. Enseguida, Wyatt Langford elevó de out al izquierdo, Corey Seager entregó el segundo tercio con fly al derecho y finalmente Josh Lung fue ponchado tirándole a una recta de 97 millas por hora.
Alex Osuna se fue de 4-2 por los Rangers de Texas
En el mismo enfrentamiento en Glob Life Field que registró asistencia de 33 mil 694 aficionados, el nativo de Los Mochis, Alejandro “Cuate” Osuna, bateó de 4-2 como quinto tolete de los Rangers de Texas.
Te podría interesar: “Se siente muy bonito”: Alex Osuna al cumplir su sueño de jugar en el Clásico Mundial de Beisbol
Osuna Quintero, de 23 años de edad, conectó su primer imparable del juego en el segundo inning ante los envíos de Spencer Miles, esto hacia el jardín central, mientras que, en la octava, el toletero zurdo volvió a pegar hit, esto ante Tyler Rogers hacia el prado izquierdo.
Brandon Valenzuela se fue de 3-1 en el triunfo de los Azulejos
El receptor originario de Hermosillo, Sonora, Brandon Valenzuela, también tuvo buena jornada este domingo al conectar un imparable en tres turnos, como octavo bat de los Azulejos de Toronto.
El bateador zurdo de 25 años de edad disparó sencillo en la sexta entrada ante el también zurdo Robert García, en un domingo de 3-1 con una base por bolas negociada.

item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays are looking to avoid being swept by the Texas Rangers on Sunday and have made some changes to their lineup.
Toronto is coming off a 6-2 loss on Saturday after losing 7-1 on Friday. The two losses seemingly ended the Blue Jays' playoff hopes.
The Blue Jays are now 76-79.
Toronto Blue Jays Announce Brandon Valenzuela News
Toronto is looking to avoid the series sweep and has made some major changes to its lineup.
The Blue Jays are resting some regular players, as starting catcher Alejandro Kirk is getting the day off, with Brandon Valenzuela getting the start. He will also be hitting eighth.
Toronto's lineup on Sunday is as follows:
- B. Bateman CF
- V. Guerrero Jr. 1B
- N. Lukes RF
- K. Okamoto 3B
- S. Keys DH
- J. Smith LF
- A. Giménez SS
- B. Valenzuela C
- E. Clement 2B
Toronto will start Spencer Miles as the opener, as it's a bullpen game with Spencer Arrighetti getting the bulk of the innings.
Kirk getting the day off isn't a surprise, as Valenzuela has been catching and starting a lot on Sunday to give Kirk the day off in the series finale.
Valenzuela is a great defensive catcher with a cannon of an arm, yet his bat has struggled as of late. He's hitting .217 with 8 home runs and 21 RBIs. However, in his last 7 games, he's hitting .105 with 0 home runs and 0 RBIs, while striking out 5 times.
Toronto Right Now
The Blue Jays have struggled all year, and now their playoff fate is likely sealed.
Toronto lost the first two games of a three-game road series against Texas, which seemingly ended their playoff hopes. The Blue Jays have been blown out in both of their games against the Rangers, which is frustrating for the team.
Jose Soriano struggled in the outing, which was frustrating for the team as the Blue Jays sent Dylan Cease and Soriano, their two best pitchers, in the first two games.
"We're still positive. Doesn't matter the result, we're still positive," said Soriano. "We're not going to win every game we play. The other team's trying to win, too. So, we try to control what we can control and play one game at a time."
The Blue Jays will go on a three-game road trip against the Baltimore Orioles starting on Monday. Toronto will end its season with a three-game home series against the Cincinnati Reds.
Toronto likely has to finish the year 7-0 to have any shot of making the playoffs.
